title: Pneumatic Retinopexy: The Minimalist's Mastery
summary: Pneumatic Retinopexy (PnR) is a minimally invasive, office-based surgical procedure for repairing primary rhegmatogenous retinal detachments (RRD) using intraocular gas and retinopexy. It offers excellent visual outcomes and avoids the morbidity of scleral buckling or vitrectomy in selected patients.

sections.title: Clinical Definition & Overview
sections.content: Pneumatic Retinopexy (PnR) is an office-based procedure involving the intravitreal injection of an expansile gas bubble (SF6 or C3F8) combined with retinopexy (cryotherapy or laser photocoagulation). It relies on the principles of surface tension and buoyancy to tamponade retinal breaks, allowing the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) pump to dehydrate the subretinal space and reattach the neurosensory retina.

sections.title: Contraindications & Red Flags
content: Inferior retinal breaks (4 o'clock to 8 o'clock)
Proliferative Vitreoretinal Retinopathy (PVR) Grade C or D
Physical/Mental inability to maintain strict positioning
Uncontrolled glaucoma (relative contraindication due to IOP spikes)
Severe media opacities (Dense vitreous heme/Cataract)
Multiple breaks spanning >1-2 clock hours

sections.title: The Step-by-Step Procedure
content: Step 1: Surgical prep (Povidone-iodine) and anesthesia (subconjunctival lidocaine).
Step 2: Pre-injection retinopexy (usually Cryotherapy) to the break(s).
Step 3: Paracentesis (AC Tap) to lower IOP, especially if injecting >0.3ml gas.
Step 4: Intravitreal injection of 0.3ml C3F8 or 0.5ml SF6 via 30G needle, 3.5-4.0mm from limbus.
Step 5: Immediate check of CRA patency (Indirect Ophthalmoscopy).
Step 6: Positioning (Head tilt to ensure bubble doesn't trap at the injection site).
Step 7: Post-operative positioning for 5-10 days (Bubble over break).

content.explanation: S: Superior breaks only. U: Unbroken view (clear media). P: Positionable patient. E: Expansile gas (SF6/C3F8). R: Retinopexy (Laser/Cryo).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Steam-roller Maneuver: If subretinal fluid (SRF) is bullous, have the patient lie face down, then slowly rotate to the desired position to 'push' fluid away from the macula.
Inverted Steam-roller: Used for superior detachments to move fluid away from the break.
Fish-egg Prevention: Inject gas with the patient's head turned so the injection site is highest; avoid 'pumping' the syringe.
Gas-Fluid Exchange: The bubble closes the break, and the RPE pump usually clears the SRF within 24-48 hours.
The 'Window' Effect: Gas allows for excellent visualization of the break for laser once the retina is flat.

sections.title: Postoperative Complications
content: New Retinal Breaks (7-15%): Most common cause of failure, usually occurring in the inferior quadrants.
Proliferative Vitreoretinal Retinopathy (PVR): Occurs in ~3-5%.
Subretinal Gas: Entry of gas into the subretinal space through the break.
Cataract progression (less common than with vitrectomy).
Delayed SRF absorption.

sections.title: The PIVOT Trial Findings
sections.content: The Pneumatic Retinopexy versus Vitrectomy for Retinal Detachment (PIVOT) Trial demonstrated that while PnR has a lower primary reattachment rate (80.6% vs 93.2%), patients in the PnR group had significantly better functional outcomes, including higher mean ETDRS visual acuity (79.9 vs 75.0 letters) and less metamorphopsia at 1 year. This 'PnR Paradox' suggests that PnR may be more gentle on the macula.

sections.title: Altitude & Travel Warnings
content: NO AIR TRAVEL until the gas bubble is completely resolved (risk of catastrophic IOP rise and CRAO).
NO Nitrous Oxide anesthesia (commonly used in dental or general surgery).
Avoid mountain passes or significant altitude changes.
Patients MUST wear a medic-alert wristband indicating intraocular gas.

sections.title: Investigations & Workup
content: 1. Dilated Scleral Depression (360 degrees) to rule out inferior breaks.
2. B-Scan Ultrasound if vitreous hemorrhage obscures the view.
3. Macular OCT to determine Macula-On vs. Macula-Off status.
4. Baseline IOP and Gonioscopy (if history of glaucoma).

rows: Persistent SRF under the primary break
SRF in a new quadrant or increasing
